title: Bahrain Refuses to Join Iran-Gulf Hormuz Talks in Oman, Citing Lack of Diplomatic Ties Since 2016
detail: Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said Manama 'will not be a party to any collective meeting that includes Iran before the resumption of diplomatic relations between the two countries,' declining to join the Monday, Sept 14 Gulf-Iran meeting in Salalah, Oman on managing Strait of Hormuz shipping. Bahrain severed ties with Iran in 2016 alongside Saudi Arabia, which restored relations in 2023; Manama has not. The ministry said regional security 'cannot be preserved through a policy of appeasement' and called for Hormuz to be open 'without discrimination, fees or permits,' pointing to the pattern of attacks on Gulf infrastructure including the Sept 10 Saudi pipeline strike. Tehran has been negotiating with Oman over a temporary Hormuz management arrangement, including a possible transit-fee mechanism Bahrain and other Gulf states oppose.

media.caption: Bahrain declines to join the Iran-Gulf Strait of Hormuz meeting in Oman, Sept 12, 2026

confidenceReason: Direct on-record statement from Bahrain's Foreign Ministry, corroborated by Al Jazeera and TASS reporting.

title: Three Iranian Security Force Members Killed in Pre-Dawn Clash With Gunmen in Saravan, Sistan-Baluchestan
detail: Iranian security forces launched an operation beginning around 4:00am local time against an armed group in Saravan, Sistan-Baluchestan province -- more than 1,300km from Tehran -- that state media said was planning a 'terrorist operation.' Three members of Iran's security forces were killed in the ensuing clashes; Iran's Revolutionary Guards said 4-5 of the gunmen were also killed, with weapons, ammunition and explosives seized. The gunmen's specific affiliation was not confirmed by state television. Security forces regularly clash with armed groups in Iran's restive southeastern border region.

media.caption: Security operation in Saravan, Sistan-Baluchestan province, Sept 12, 2026
